messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
the problem moves somewhere else instead of disappearing while you are handling A fault-finding test. Putting everything back would waste a lot of effort. How do you approach it?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "I rub my palm and take the test paper. \"I put it back,\" I say. I scrape the fault edge once, then look at the mark. I say, \"leave it here. I mark it wrong. I mark the fault again.\" I put the paper back, scrape once more, and say, \"no,\" but I leave the fault mark alone."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i put the wrench down. i put it back. i check the test. i leave the wrench in the corner. i leave the test."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I keep the test bag on my lap and look at the fault. Then I put the bag back and listen for the sound of my hand moving. “Maybe the test went wrong,” I say."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i keep the test pocket beside the broken part and trace the edge with my thumbnail. i leave the fault-finding diagram beside the test, but i move the pocket twice because the edge feels smaller. i put a pencil mark beside the test and leave the pocket empty."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "I take the test away and put the rusted gear in the pocket. “I put the test in the wrong order. the fault is in the wrong place.” I leave the gear in the test case and watch the test fail. the failure is not a pattern, not a sequence."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i put the test case beside the sand and leave the sand where it lies. the fault comes back. i put my hand near the test and mark the spot with a pencil. the rest can wait."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "1. check the fault. 2. check the test. 3. check the watch. slow. 4. check the ruler. 5. i mark the place. 6. check the dust. 7. put the test back. 8. ask the watch for the day. 9. i keep it tidy."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "I move one drawer. The drawer is wrong. I put the wrong piece in the wrong drawer. I check the label. No—the label says wrong. I put the drawer back. Then I move the drawer again. I keep the test. I keep the sequence."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i rub my palm and set the test aside. i move the test away from the bench and test the fault-finding part. if the test moves, i stop and keep the fault-finding part aside. i mark the test's position and try again."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i put the test back on the table, then put the ruler beside it. the ruler stays on the table, so i put the ruler back on the table again. the fault goes somewhere else. i move the ruler back and put the test back."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i tap the test file twice, then write the fault on the wrong side. “the wrong side,” i say, and put the test in a drawer beside the file. i test the fault once on the wrong side, then leave the drawer empty and write the test on the nearest scrap."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i put the test case back and mark the fault with a pencil. “i know the test moved, i still write the fault in the test.” i leave the test in the drawer. “if i find a piece of evidence, i keep it.”"}]
